receipt.public_excerpt: it sold all 32.1 million shares it held in Nvidia last month, raising $5.83 billion. It also offloaded part of its stake in the wireless carrier T-Mobile USA Inc. for $9.17 billion. The sale, along with money raised from a recent margin loan on SoftBank’s holding in the British chip designer Arm Holdings Plc, will help provide much needed cash for the company’s commitment to OpenAI

evidence_items.explanation: SoftBank's own earnings disclosure, as reported, shows it sold valuable stakes (all of its Nvidia shares and part of T-Mobile) and borrowed against Arm shares to fund the OpenAI commitment. This is the route the claim said would be needed.

receipt.public_excerpt: it took on an additional $27 billion in debt in the last three months of the year, including debt at its subsidiaries. It also sold over $3.5 billion in shares of T-Mobile, on top of the previously announced $5.8 billion it raised by selling a stake in Nvidia.

evidence_items.explanation: Reports SoftBank's disclosure that it took on $27 billion of new debt in Q4 2025 and sold more stakes, and that this cash helped pay the $22.5 billion OpenAI investment. This is significant new debt plus asset sales.

metric_scope.metric: New debt and asset sales funding OpenAI investment

receipt.public_excerpt: SoftBank CFO Yoshimitsu Goto said Thursday the company's debt amounts to just 20% of the total value of SoftBank's assets -- a more conservative borrowing policy SoftBank developed after prior tech busts scared investors.

evidence_items.explanation: SoftBank's view that its borrowing stayed within a conservative loan-to-value limit. This speaks to whether the debt was risky, not to whether new debt and stake sales were needed.
